subject: Audit & Access Log archival / export options — clarifying retention windows
messages:
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Audit/access logs — retention and export questions

Hi Marcus,

We're working through our audit evidence collection for a customer audit and have two quick questions about Redwood's audit and access logs:

1) What retention windows do you offer for audit (admin actions, config changes) versus access (API key usage, token-level access) logs? Are there hard limits by plan or can we request extended retention for specific accounts?

2) For exports: can we trigger ad-hoc exports of a chosen time range (e.g., 90 days) as CSV with full metadata (timestamp, actor id, actor email, action, resource id, region, request id)? If so, what is the expected time-to-complete for a 30–90 day export for a mid-sized org (10k requests/day)?

We may need the CSV for our SOC auditor next week. Appreciate a concise runbook and any sample export file you can share.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Ross
Senior Security Analyst — Acme Corp
security-ops@acme-corp.com

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-10T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit/access logs — retention and export questions

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Grace (Security) and Lauren (Platform Ops) for the technical details and runbook. High-level answers below; I'll follow up with an export sample and timeline.

Short answers:
- Retention: default hosted retention is 180 days for audit logs, 90 days for access logs. Extended retention (custom contracts) can be provisioned up to 3 years for audit logs and 1 year for access logs under Dedicated or Private plans.
- Exports: yes — we support ad-hoc exports of arbitrary time ranges as CSV/NDJSON with full metadata. For a 30–90 day export at ~10k reqs/day we estimate 2–6 hours for CSV generation on Hosted (depends on concurrency); Dedicated customers can get priority export jobs and faster window (often <1 hour).

I'll attach a sanitized sample CSV and a short runbook. Grace/ Lauren: can you add confirmation on SLA for export job durations and any rate limits to surface to Acme's auditors?

Best,
Marcus

--

Subject: Re: Audit/access logs — retention and export questions

Emily,

Thanks for the note. A few additional details and constraints from Security side:

- Log types and retention:
  * Audit (admin/config actions): default 180 days on Hosted, configurable up to 1095 days (3 years) on Dedicated/Private.
  * Access (API key usage, token-level events): default 90 days on Hosted, configurable up to 365 days on Dedicated/Private.
  * Billing/usage metrics are summarized separately and retained per billing policy.

- Export fields: our CSV includes timestamp (UTC), internal_actor_id, actor_email (when available), action, resource_type, resource_id, ip_address (if not masked by privacy config), request_id, region, request_payload_ref. PII is redacted by default; we can produce a PII-inclusive export under an established DPA addendum and logged approval.

- Ad-hoc export workflow:
  1) Customer files an export request via Support or Console (choose range, log types, output format).
  2) Job is queued; estimate provided in the UI and via ticket.
  3) Once generated, a secure download link (short-lived) is posted to the ticket and optionally S3/presigned URL delivery can be configured for Dedicated instances.

- Performance guidance: our Hosted infra processes ~10–50M events/hour in aggregate; for an individual customer at 10k events/day, a 90-day export is light (≈900k rows) and should typically complete in 1–3 hours. Heavy exports that require rehydrating archived blocks (beyond default retention) incur longer delays.

- Deletion / retention enforcement: retention is enforced via automated lifecycle jobs. When a customer requests deletion within the retention window (e.g., user-delete requests), we mark records and purge them according to policy; fully completed deletions are auditable via a deletion job record.

I'll attach our short export runbook and a sanitized example row. Marcus / Lauren -- please confirm the secure transfer options for Acme's compliance team.

Grace
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Audit/access logs — retention and export questions

Emily — quick ops summary and runbook steps you can hand to auditors:

Runbook (ad-hoc export via Console or Support ticket):
1) Create export: Console -> Observability -> Logs -> Export -> select date range & types -> format (CSV/NDJSON).
2) Validate: We validate parameters and check retention coverage (if requested window > provisioned retention we surface granularity & archive rehydration cost).
3) Job scheduling: On Hosted, job enters shared export queue; expected ETA is shown. On Dedicated / Private, you can request high-priority job with SLA.
4) Delivery: secure download link (HTTPS, short-lived). For Dedicated, we can push to your S3 bucket using pre-signed PUT if you provide the bucket ARN/role.
5) Verification: sample row count and MD5 checksum provided; we include a manifest describing columns and any redaction logic.

Notes / caveats:
- If you need unredacted fields (IP addresses, full request payload), please attach the signed DPA addendum in the ticket and allow additional time for legal review.
- Large export or concurrent exports may face throttling; we'll surface that in the ticket ETA.

Dylan, please confirm the export concurrency limit for Hosted and whether we can guarantee under 3 hours for 900k rows for Acme's org size.

Thanks,
Lauren
Platform Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@acme-corp.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-12T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit/access logs — retention and export questions

Emily — quick operational confirmation:

- Hosted concurrency: export jobs processed with up to 4 worker threads per customer in the shared queue. At ~10k events/day (≈900k rows for 90 days) we consistently see job times 45min–2.5hr depending on system load. So the 1–3 hour window Grace mentioned is conservative and safe for planning with auditors.
- For Dedicated: we can allocate 16 workers and push the job under 30–45 minutes for the same dataset if requested in ticket with priority SLA.
- Delivery options: console download (HTTPS), presigned S3 PUT to your bucket (we require a role ARN), or a secure SFTP transfer (requires scheduling).

If you confirm the export window you want (start/end dates) and whether you need unredacted fields, we'll open the export job and provide ETA + download link.

Regards,
Dylan
Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
